newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian officials see 1997 gold output at 95-110 T.
newsitem.headline: Russian officials see 1997 gold output at 95-110 T.

text.p: Senior Russian gold industry officials variously forecast on Thursday that Russia's 1997 gold output would be in the range of 95 to 110 tonnes.

The officials gave Reuters their estimates at an industry conference. Russia's 1996 gold output is variously estimated by the Industry Ministry, the Central Bank and the State Statistics Committee to have been 124 tonnes, 122 tonnes or 100.8 tonnes, respectively.
"My figure (for 1997) is 95 tonnes," said Valery Rudakov, president of the Evrozoloto financial-industrial group.

Valery Braiko, chairman of the Union of Gold Industrialists, said some new mining capacity had come on stream at the end of last year and beginning of this year. "Output in 1997 will be flat (on 1996) at 105-100 tonnes," he said.
Viktor Tarakanovsky, chairman of the board of the Gold Prospectors' Union, said: "Last year's output was 112-113 tonnes, and I'm inclined to think it will be at least 95 to 100 tonnes this year."
Vladimir Piskunov, president of the Russian Diamond Union, said, "We expect 110 tonnes."

None of the officials knew anything of recent market talk that Russian Central Bank officials might meet Japanese trading houses in Tokyo to discuss issuing Russian government bonds backed by Russian gold.
They also knew nothing of recent market rumours that Russia might be in talks with Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) to swap gold for platinum and palladium.

The Central Bank said at the end of January that it had around 400 tonnes of gold in its reserves, including reserves acquired from the Goskhran, or Gosfond, strategic pile. The bank has said it aims this year and next to boost its reserves by 90 tonnes a year. --Julie Tolkacheva, Moscow Newsroom, +7095 941 8520
